title: A capability carried onward
scope: Proposed execution plan against the live spine. Source inventory headings, curated hall choices and inspected opening evidence; not a claim of 207 tested lessons.

sequences.aim: Make a running world available for construction: distinguish execution, position, frame, relation, record, representation, connectivity, generating rule and finite limit; compose with what those distinctions permit.
sequences.carry: Reuse PointBody and CubeBody recipes, independent resources, local/world frames, retained records and face connections. A saved drawing, a class and a live node are different kinds of continuity. Carry placement versus construction into Transformation, using familiar bodies to study change through time.
sequences.check: Offer an independent arrangement using generated positions, a preserved source and altered copy, a valid indexed face and two sphere resolutions. Ask for predictions, execution and an explanation of the choices. The exercise is assigned; independent learner understanding has not been observed.
sequences.note: 6 October: all fifteen Primitives tutorial/final pairs exist; Trace → Grid and the nine later learner programs have native evidence. Consolidate this chapter rather than restart it. For each comparison ask BRING / CHANGE / KEEP / LEARN / TEST / CARRY. Mark concept roles supplied, introduced, practised, or independently demonstrated with evidence; supplied syntax is not mastery. Takeaways: /book-review/doc/book/iterations/2026-10-06-what-the-next-room-keeps/notes.html. Next: inspect Transformation using the familiar sphere/cube. Keep reflection and runnable reconstruction distinct; sequence order remains editable.

sequences.aim: Choose translation, rotation and scale; explain what each preserves and what it changes in the space available to a body.
sequences.carry: Whole BoxMesh construction, deliberate transform properties, parent-child scope, overlap detection and a solid composed opening. Arrays returns to still collectible cubes with addresses; no live-node transport is assumed.
sequences.check: Predict and make a changed pose or opening; identify the operation, frame and preserved properties. Test its timing or input only where used.
sequences.note: Seven canonical tutorial constructions reconciled from reviewed drafts and freshly tested 12 October. Current final texts preserved. Pre → crossings → journey → pivot → scale → approach → solid opening. Read TRANSFORMATION_SUMMARIES.md. Arrays is the next separate pass.

sequences.aim: Address and change many independent things.
sequences.carry: Whole cube construction → independent copies and retained slots → declared YZX volume → address-to-turn rule → saved image on another receiver → score with separate clock. Values, references, orientation and events stay distinct; Colour continues with familiar geometry and per-instance materials.
sequences.check: Change one stored value and one object through their indices, preserving unrelated entries; explain aliasing.
sequences.note: Five canonical tutorials complete for this pass, using the reviewed Array draft and four new minimal constructions. Seven printed files; fresh 451 native checks and 15 rejected faults. Walls loads Floor output in a separate engine process. Current final.md and runtime unchanged. Read ARRAYS_SUMMARIES.md. Colour is next.

sequences.aim: Separate a calculated value, its receiver and its retained state.
sequences.carry: Arrays addresses → material assignments → illumination → position-to-colour → ordered bands → sampled HSV field → Palette state → retained surface marks → independent panes. Familiar PointBody and Palette return unchanged; numerical handoffs are explicit records. Pattern_Disco next separates pattern from palette.
sequences.check: Create two independent palettes, advance one, and apply a returned colour to a new receiver; explain the surface-painting states.
sequences.note: Eight canonical tutorials now incorporate the reviewed drafts. 21 printed files; 811 native assertions, 39 render checks and 27 rejected faults. Grid/Walls have supplied museum pointer controls; Paint manual-first and Rainbow optional. Current reflections and live museum preserved. See COLOUR_SUMMARIES.md. Text remains revisable.

sequences.aim: Separate a source from its repeated interpretations.
sequences.carry: Colour PointBody, Palette and GridSurface → independent palette/phase → source entries → reflected reads → physical frames → glide → copied recipes → optional volume → controlled comparison → UV sampling and a saved garment recipe.
sequences.check: Predict a source address and all its visible occurrences. Keep source values fixed while changing one reader operation; distinguish this from editing or copying the source.
sequences.note: All nine full tutorials and Ribbon companions exist. Current 9–10 October loom and garment revisions preserved. Most entry scripts initialize declared state; reuse is not automatic saved-state transfer. Optional loom cloth is explicitly saved for the cutting table. The five-column preview cuts a six-column reflected period short; a wider view remains a proposed spatial improvement. See TILING_SUMMARIES.md. Accepted execution scope; revisable text.

sequences.aim: Distinguish a difference, a rate and an accumulated change.
sequences.carry: The line difference and trace return as measurements of the familiar sphere's positions, a sampled curve and a followed field. Name frame, time interval and units; carry a measurable motion into Forces.
sequences.check: Compare finite differences and finite sums at two step sizes, with units and a retained source.
sequences.note: Field-following assigns a prescribed velocity here. Forces later stores velocity and changes it through acceleration.

sequences.aim: Distinguish a relation, a prescribed path and forces acting on retained state.
sequences.carry: The familiar sphere gains velocity, force response, drag, spring attachment and pair interaction; the cube returns for support; the player becomes the final receiver.
sequences.check: Predict one independent change in each focused reconstruction, then compare the actual engine response.
sequences.note: Eleven current halls remain in order. One primary reconstruction per hall, several brief vector readings in the compact opening. Phase rods stay primary because their contrast with springs matters. 8 October tested code and real museum evidence; physical headset review remains open.

sequences.aim: Change parameters by a criterion rather than draw a desired result directly.
sequences.carry: A body or curve becomes a candidate, evaluated and revised under constraints.
sequences.check: Change a step size or boundary and distinguish convergence, a limit and a failed search.
sequences.note: Annealing needs a small bounded-draw preview before Randomness. Keep current state, best state and evaluator separate.

sequences.aim: Read periodic change in position, time and coupled state.
sequences.carry: A familiar sphere receives periodic position or pulse changes; amplitude, period and phase deepen the earlier motion rule. Carry a reusable oscillator toward catalyst behaviours, then distinguish that body from a sampled wave or coupled field.
sequences.check: Predict amplitude, period and phase changes; combine two known signals and explain the sampling limits.
sequences.note: This sequence owns the unit circle and sine derivation. Sound output, spatial clearance and wave coupling are distinct receivers.

sequences.aim: Make chance reproducible and examine distributions and consequences.
sequences.carry: A rule and seed produce samples, walks, populations and feedback.
sequences.check: Replay a saved recipe; change draw order and compare distributions without claiming identical outcomes across engines.
sequences.note: A short random call can precede this sequence. Here teach the generator, draw order, distributions, sampling policies and inference.

sequences.aim: Sample related values and distinguish the field from its display.
sequences.carry: The sampler drives points, occupancy, skin and route comparisons.
sequences.check: Hold sample positions fixed while changing a generator setting; compare neighbour differences and preserve original values.
sequences.note: Do not infer continuity from smooth colour. Spatial spacing, threshold and domain warp are separate choices.

sequences.aim: Run a small spatial rule for every fragment.
sequences.carry: Known distance, colour, tiling and noise rules move onto a surface.
sequences.check: Write a distance mask, repeat its coordinates, then specify the previous-state input needed to turn a recomputed image into a retained simulation. Do not claim the current display supplies working feedback.
sequences.note: Use The Book of Shaders as an inspiration for operations, translated to Godot. GPU feedback storage is not automatic. Four lessons are missing.

sequences.aim: Give a local rule a stored state and a generation boundary.
sequences.carry: The grid gains current/next buffers, neighbours and recorded generations.
sequences.check: Update a tiny known state by hand, then match it in code; reverse traversal order and preserve the result.
sequences.note: Hall names do not certify algorithms. Verify actual installed rules before calling a specimen elementary CA or Life.

sequences.aim: Describe repeated construction with a stopping rule.
sequences.carry: Known lists and functions become recursive branches and replacement histories.
sequences.check: Predict growth at a small depth and impose a node budget; distinguish recursion depth from physical size.
sequences.note: A visible fractal is not evidence of infinity. Keep base cases and finite budgets explicit.

sequences.aim: Separate rewriting a description from interpreting it.
sequences.carry: A word, stack and recipe construct a branching body.
sequences.check: Rewrite a short word in parallel; copy/restore turtle state at a branch and inspect the resulting connections.
sequences.note: Dictionaries, strings and stacks need explicit small introductions. Shape grammar is currently a missing lesson, not a prerequisite for all growth.

sequences.aim: Keep the representation, evaluator and construction rule visible.
sequences.carry: Candidate records and branch/voxel records generate selections and passages.
sequences.check: Change a fitness criterion or growth condition and explain which candidates or connections it excludes.
sequences.note: Add minimal adjacency at the first network use; Graph Theory later formalizes traversal. Full graph theory need not be moved forward.

sequences.aim: Distinguish a deformable state from the constraints applied to it.
sequences.carry: Mesh vertices and forces become a constrained sheet, pressure body or coupled field.
sequences.check: Hold material and load fixed while changing pinned boundaries; explain solver response versus an authored animation.
sequences.note: Teach a bounded constraint experiment; do not reproduce the full cloth solver in the first lesson.

sequences.aim: Turn sampled scalar values into a chosen boundary.
sequences.carry: A field and a threshold produce a surface and a clearance test.
sequences.check: Classify one cell, interpolate one crossing, then vary level without mutating samples.
sequences.note: Extraction tables are supplied first. Continuous description, finite samples and walkable collision remain distinct.

sequences.aim: Compose solids with ordered set operations.
sequences.carry: Known forms become operands and inhabitable differences.
sequences.check: Swap A−B and B−A; compare with union/intersection and test passage separately from appearance.
sequences.note: Boolean logic already exists. CSG adds solid representations and noncommutative difference, not a fresh introduction to if.

sequences.aim: Distinguish where coordination lives: shared trace, supplied direction, neighbourhood, individual state, paired channels, evaluated memory and continuing support.
sequences.carry: Keep the point and explicit update records. Carry selected relations and their conditions into Graph Theory; Machine Learning follows.
sequences.check: Predict one agent update, then compare traversal orders and neighbourhoods in a small population.
sequences.note: Seek/flee/arrive are candidate small studies in the Boids hall; pursuit/evade may remain optional. Do not claim the current lesson already contains them.

sequences.aim: Separate identity and connectivity from drawing positions.
sequences.carry: Known relation records become adjacency, traversals and constrained allocations.
sequences.check: Reconstruct a route from predecessors; test an unreachable target; move the layout without changing connectivity.
sequences.note: Own queues, visit order, predecessors, distance costs and an admissible heuristic before machine learning. Preserve reflective returns to earlier relation structures.

sequences.aim: Separate prediction, error and parameter updates.
sequences.carry: An evaluated candidate becomes a model with data, loss and learned weights.
sequences.check: Train on one declared sample set and evaluate on held-out cases; explain what the score cannot establish.
sequences.note: Graph Theory now precedes this sequence. Return to directed computations and distinguish activations from learned weights. Clustering is not supervised classification; existing lessons still need alignment and tested hosts.

sequences.aim: Distinguish a finite computation, an assumption and a warranted claim.
sequences.carry: Known programs become experiments on geometry, membership and proof checking.
sequences.check: State what a bounded experiment establishes and what it cannot prove; change an assumption explicitly.
sequences.note: Several halls should be reflective investigations with tiny witnesses, not grand algorithms that supposedly demonstrate entire theorems.

sequences.aim: Inspect a proposed research model and its measurement choices.
sequences.carry: Retained observations become weighted expressions and revisable experiments.
sequences.check: Preserve inputs, vary one weight, compare a stated measure and record the interpretive limit.
sequences.note: QFEP is the project’s research proposal. Do not promote a convenient scalar or metaphor into an established physical law.

sequences.aim: Make a revisable work with accountable records and other people.
sequences.carry: Known objects, relations and recipes become situated assemblies and recoverable versions.
sequences.check: Compose an original work, retain its source/decisions and explain whose observations or participation are absent.
sequences.note: This is synthesis and critical reflection. Do not add new compulsory syntax simply to make every hall a lesson.

lessons.change:
`b.position - a.position` gives the movement from a to b in the study’s local coordinates. Its three components tell us how far to move along each axis. `length()` measures the whole gap.

Divide that displacement by its length to keep only direction. The result has length one. When the points meet, the `if` leaves direction at zero: there is no direction to recover from a zero-length gap.

Read the projection last. `dot(Vector3.RIGHT)` takes the signed X component. Multiplying it by `Vector3.RIGHT` makes a vector along X; subtracting it from the full displacement leaves the remainder. Add the two parts and you get the original displacement back. This is another use of vector addition.

lessons.change:
Read `at(t)` from left to right. `START` is the departure position. `initial_velocity * t` is the displacement that the initial velocity would produce on its own. With `(3, 4, 0)`, the point begins by moving right at 3 m/s and up at 4 m/s.

The last term, `0.5 * acceleration * t * t`, adds the effect of constant downward acceleration. As time grows, this term bends the flight downward. Its units are metres, so all three terms can be added.

FIRE sets time to zero and starts the updates. Each frame adds `delta` to time and asks `at(time)` for a position. `duration()` finds when this particular flight returns to its starting height; `minf` stops the clock at that instant.

lessons.object: Use three instances of the familiar point. Give each the same force for the same time and vary only mass. The supplied `free_point.gd` lets them move freely, with gravity and damping set to zero.
lessons.change:
`Point.new()` makes another instance of the class you already built. `points.append(point)` keeps the body itself in the array; Trace kept positions. The index `i` supplies its placement and mass. `pow(2.0, i)` gives 1, 2 and 4 for indices 0, 1 and 2.

`apply_central_force` supplies a push to the rigid body. Godot updates its velocity and position. A greater mass receives a smaller acceleration from the same force. For a constant force, acceleration is force divided by mass; the velocity change is force × duration ÷ mass. One newton acting for one second changes these bodies’ speeds by 1, 0.5 and 0.25 m/s, starting from rest and before contact.

`_physics_process(delta)` is the new callback here. Godot calls it at the physics update rate; `delta` is the duration of one such step in seconds. Use it to apply a continuing force. The engine integrates that force during the step.

The loop visits every point. While `remaining` is positive, it applies the force to points that are not held. The clock keeps counting down during a grab, so a held point misses that part of the push. Once time runs out, the code stops applying force. It never sets velocity back to zero.

The button connects to `push()`. Pressing it sets the shared clock to one second. Wait for one pulse to end before comparing a second: pressing during a pulse restarts its remaining time.

lessons.change:
`flat` is the point’s position in the study’s horizontal X–Z plane. Multiplying it by a negative number gives an inward vector toward the centre.

`Vector3(-flat.z, 0, flat.x)` turns that vector sideways by a quarter-turn. Normalizing gives it unit length; multiplying by 2.8 sets the sideways acceleration. Add this to the inward part to make the swirl.

Each physics update samples again at the point’s new position. `global_basis` turns the local result into world axes. Then `point.mass * acceleration` supplies the force needed for that acceleration. The point keeps its existing velocity as this new contribution acts.

lessons.change:
The `if` asks whether the point is inside the height range. Outside it, this script adds no resistance. Inside it, the force opposes `linear_velocity`.

Start with the minus sign in `resistance()`: it reverses the velocity’s direction. Multiplying by `velocity.length()` makes faster motion meet stronger resistance. Double the speed and the force becomes four times as large, before the limit is reached.

`coefficient` controls the strength of that resistance. Gravity continues to pull down while drag opposes the fall. DROP unfreezes the point so the engine can begin this exchange.

lessons.object: Make one spring from the familiar point and a fixed anchor. In your small study, grab the point itself to set its position, then release it to see the spring act. The thin cylinder shows the attachment.
lessons.change:
`offset` points from the body to the anchor. Its length tells us their current separation. Subtract `rest_length` to find how far the spring is stretched or compressed.

Multiplying that difference by `stiffness` gives the force magnitude. The normalized offset gives its direction. A stretched spring pulls toward the anchor; compression reverses the sign.

`angles` stores where each arm is in its turn. `rates` stores how much angle it gains per second. `TAU` is one full turn, so `TAU / 6` completes it in six seconds.

lessons.object: Extend the familiar point into a thruster. While held and activated, it reports an acceleration in the direction of your hand. The small station script creates two of these points.
lessons.change:
`action_pressed` turns firing on while the point is held. Releasing the trigger or dropping the point turns it off. `held()` reports whether someone has picked it up.

`receiver()` follows the holding controller to its XR origin, then finds the player body under that origin. This connects the action to the player whose hand holds the point.

`acceleration()` reads the controller’s forward direction, local -Z, and multiplies it by 11 m/s². When firing stops, it returns zero. It does not clear the player’s velocity.

Adding the point to `ada_thrust_points` lets the existing court find it. The court asks each held point who its receiver is and what acceleration it requests. Two aligned points request 22 m/s²; opposed directions cancel. The court combines those requests, adds gravity once and moves the player with collisions.
